intro: Before you rise the bow-fronted, whitewashed houses of Beypazarı, a historic town in Ankara province from the 18th–19th century. It lay on the Ankara branch of the Silk Road, and it is one of the few Anatolian towns restored and kept whole rather than house by house.
history: The town was a stop and a market on the branch of the Silk Road that ran through Ankara. Its houses, timber-framed, filled with mud-brick and whitewashed, were built in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Then, from the 1990s, a restoration programme preserved the streets as a whole. It is one of the few cases in Anatolia where the fabric of a town, rather than individual buildings, was saved.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the bow-fronted mansions, the old market, the Rüstem Pasha Baths and the Kurşunlu Mosque.
facts: Did you know? The eighty-layer baklava the town is known for is a gift of its climate: here the dough can be rolled thinner and drier. And Beypazarı is one of the few places in Anatolia where the whole fabric, rather than individual buildings, was saved.
outro: This brings our tour of Beypazarı Houses to an end. Before you go, please leave the old houses untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
